headline: Universal Music Group has signed a multi-year deal with the AI voice company ElevenLabs to build a licensed music remix platform for fans.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 6: a licensing deal by a major label, announced by both companies, with few terms disclosed.
importance_line: What changed is that a major record label chose to license its music for AI remixing with one company while it is still suing another, which matters to artists and songwriters, who must opt in, and to fans who could legally remix, then to the labels and AI firms, and the doubt is that the report gives no launch date, price or payment terms.
summary: Billboard reports that Universal Music Group (UMG) and ElevenLabs, an AI audio company, will build a platform where fans can remix and mash up music from artists and songwriters who choose to take part, on licensed music; ElevenLabs' chief executive says artists will be "fairly compensated". The deal leaves out ElevenLabs' existing music products and comes a day after rival Suno launched models trained with music from UMG's competitors, while UMG and Sony Music are still suing Suno over alleged copyright infringement.
